drafted_from: tool row in tools/connected-drives/tool-rows.json, read-data/drives.mjs and test/drives.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Get the Finder icon of my SAMPLE DRIVE as a 64 pixel picture." It runs tool:get-a-drive-icon with mount /Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE and size 64 and hands back the PNG as base64.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads the drives this computer shows and changes nothing.
instructions: 1. Run tool:list-connected-drives and copy the mount of the drive.
2. Say "Get the icon of /Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE at 64 pixels"; the AI calls tools:run for tool:get-a-drive-icon with mount and size (32 to 512; 256 when left out).
3. Read media_type (image/png) and base64; decode base64 to a PNG file to show it. A size outside 32 to 512 is refused.
4. A computer that draws no drive icons answers {mount, icon: "none", reason} instead.

worked_examples.title: Draw a 64 pixel drive icon
worked_examples.ask: Get the Finder icon of my SAMPLE DRIVE as a 64 pixel picture.
worked_examples.given: From tools/connected-drives/test/drives.test.mjs (draws a drive icon at an allowed size only): the icon is drawn by osascript with the mount and 64 as arguments; the test stands in 9 bytes of text for the picture, a real run writes a PNG.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"mount":"/Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE","media_type":"image/png","base64":"iVBORw0KGgo..."} (base64 of the PNG file the computer drew; size 4 would be refused with "from 32 to 512").
